      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Incident Ops Synthesis and Customer Commitment Kit\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-ops-synthesis-and-customer-commitment-kit-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\n-to-first-mitigation <=20 min, p95 recovery to within 2x baseline within 30 min.\n\nStatus page and customer communication templates\n- Principles: be fast, factual, and actionable. Avoid speculation; give an ETA for next update. Use the phrase \"investigating\" until mitigation verified.\n\nTemplate A — Initial public status (short):\nTitle: Degraded performance affecting inference endpoints\\Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or errors.\\Current status: Investigating — we are seeing elevated error rates for traffic routed to us-east-1 queues.\\Next update: in 30 minutes.\nAdvice for customers: If you use region pinned hosts, consider switching to us-west-2 as a temporary workaround. Contact support@redwood.ai for account-specific assistance.\n\nTemplate B — Account-specific email (when known impact):\n\\Subject: Redwood status update — temporary performance degradation for <customer-name>\\Hi <CS Rep> / <Customer Contact>,\\We are investigating elevated error rates affecting requests for your account. Our engineers have applied a routing mitigation and are monitoring.\\What we’re doing: scaled dedicated pool for your tenant and moved traffic to encrypted-us-west-2 nodes.\\Action for you: no action required unless you continue to see errors. If you prefer, we can coordinate a manual failover at a scheduled time.\\Estimated next update: <ETA>\n\nTemplate C — Post-incident customer closing note and remediation offer:\n\\Subject: Incident resolved — summary and remediation options for <customer-name>\\Hi <Customer Contact>,\\Summary: On <date> we experienced a performance degradation caused by <root-cause>. The service was fully restored at <time>.\\Impact: Your account experienced ~X% additional latency and Y failed requests during the incident window.\\What we fixed: <short list of technical remediations>.\\Compensation: We will credit <X>% of the affected usage billed in <month> per our SLA. Please let your CS rep know if you require additional evidence.\\Next steps: we scheduled a targeted follow-up with your team to discuss longer-term mitigations.\\nRegards,\\Customer Success / Incident Response",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Incident Ops Synthesis and Customer Commitment Kit\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-ops-synthesis-and-customer-commitment-kit-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\n>.\\Compensation: We will credit <X>% of the affected usage billed in <month> per our SLA. Please let your CS rep know if you require additional evidence.\\Next steps: we scheduled a targeted follow-up with your team to discuss longer-term mitigations.\\nRegards,\\Customer Success / Incident Response\n\nPostmortem template (required fields):\n- Title\n- Incident ID\n- Severity\n- Start / End times (UTC)\n- Affected services and customers\n- Detecting signal(s)\n- Root cause (one-paragraph)\n- Timeline of events (minute-level bullets)\n- Mitigations applied (short list)\n- Corrective action(s) and owners (include ETA)\n- Follow-up validations and telemetry to add\n- Blameless summary and learnings\n\nExample timeline excerpt (format):\n- 2026-02-10T14:03Z — Pager triggered: router p95 > 1500ms\n- 2026-02-10T14:05Z — Bridge opened; IL assigned: @marisol. Initial post to status page.\n- 2026-02-10T14:16Z — Scale-up of dedicated pool in us-west-2 completed.\n- 2026-02-10T14:42Z — p95 returned to baseline; monitoring stable.\n\nSLOs and evidence collection (minimum):\n- SLOs to monitor: request p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, queue depth, and head-of-line latency.\n- Evidence archive: bridge log (transcript), snapshots of dashboards, relevant kube logs (kubectl logs with timestamps), and saved tracer spans (jaeger link).\n- Retention: put incident evidence into the incident-bucket with path: s3://incident-evidence/<incident-id>/ and tag the runbook entry.\n\nEscalation matrix (short bullets):\n- If unresolved after 30 min: escalate to service owner and SRE lead.\n- If unresolved after 3 hours OR customer credit threshold met: notify CTO and Customer Success SVP.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Incident Ops Synthesis and Customer Commitment Kit\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-ops-synthesis-and-customer-commitment-kit-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: oncall-and-incident-response\n\n3://incident-evidence/<incident-id>/ and tag the runbook entry.\n\nEscalation matrix (short bullets):\n- If unresolved after 30 min: escalate to service owner and SRE lead.\n- If unresolved after 3 hours OR customer credit threshold met: notify CTO and Customer Success SVP.\n\nSLA credit decision ladder (summary):\n- If cross-tenant SLO > 30 minutes in a billing month, trigger auto-review for credit.\n- Manual exceptions handled by Finance & Legal in coordination with CS.\n\nRunbook hygiene and governance:\n- Runbooks must be <700 words and contain 3 quick mitigations.\n- Each service runbook is reviewed quarterly by the owner and during each major release.\n- Retire or archive runbooks older than 18 months unless owner reaffirms relevance.\n\nAppendix: useful CLI snippets and queries\n- Basic health: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .\n- Resource checks: redwoodctl nodes list --region=us-east-1 --format=json | jq '.nodes | length'\n- Traces: jaeger query --service <svc> --start <ISO-8601> --end <ISO-8601>\n\nAppendix: decision record for customer notifications (short)\n- Decision: Use conservative, repeated short updates (every 30–60 minutes) rather than infrequent long updates.\n- Rationale: Frequent updates reduce inbound support load and increase customer trust.\n\nContact matrix (oncall distribution):\n- Primary oncall: weekly rotation; backup: weekly rotation offset by one. For critical holidays, create a 2-person escalation pair.\n\nRevision history:\n- 2026-02-15 — created by Marisol Chen (first draft).\n- 2026-03-01 — reviewed and published after SRE and CS review.\n\nRelated artifacts and templates: copy these into your service folder as link references:\n- canonical-runbook-template.md\n- incident-evidence-archive-template.yml\n- statuspage-templates-v2.md\n\nTitle Field Name: title\n\n## Content Field Names\n\n- content",

document.title: Incident Ops Synthesis and Customer Commitment Kit
document.content:
{
  "title": "Incident Ops Synthesis and Customer Commitment Kit",
  "space": "oncall-and-incident-response",
  "author": "Marisol Chen",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-03-01",
  "reviewers": [
    "Ethan Jones",
    "Priya Nair",
    "Liam O'Connor"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "incident-ops",
    "customer-comms",
    "runbooks",
    "slo",
    "game-day"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-comm-and-postmortem-framework-2026.json",
    "/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/2025"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "Summary:
This document collates the core incident lifecycle guidance, runbook templates, on-call rotation patterns, game-day play outlines, and customer-facing status templates we use to fulfill commitments when Redwood experiences service disruptions. It is intended for SREs, service owners, customer success, and on-call engineers.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Applies to all public-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, dedicated pools) and control-plane services that impact customer request routing, billing, or data access.
- Intent: Reduce time-to-stabilize, make customer communication predictable and clear, and ensure post-incident learning drives improvements to SLOs and runbooks.

Quick reference: roles and responsibilities
1) Incident Lead (IL) — generally the oncall SRE or service owner. Owns timeline, decisions, and customer brief cadence.
2) Bridge Operator — runs the war-room (Zoom/MS Teams), snapshots evidence, posts updates to the status page.
3) Tier-1 Responder — initial triage, short-term mitigations, tooling to mute noisy alerts.
4) Tier-2/3 Engineers — deep debugging, remediation, and config changes.
5) Customer Success Liaison — crafts external messaging and liaises with affected accounts.
6) Postmortem Owner — writes the retrospective, tracks action items.

Incident classification matrix (short):
- Sev 1: Global outage affecting >25% customers or system-level SLO breach >30 mins. Requires immediate IL, exec notification.
- Sev 2: Partial degradation impacting specific features or regions with measurable SLO regression. Notify affected customers within 60 min.
- Sev 3: Minor or isolated issues with limited customer impact; handled in normal oncall cadence.

Incident lifecycle (detailed run-loop):
1) Detection & initial triage (0-5 min)
   - Pager fires; Tier-1 responder acknowledges in 5 min.
   - Collect these 3 data points within first 10 minutes: symptom (error/latency), blast radius (tenants/regions), and possible choke points (GPU pool, autoscaler, network).
2) Mobilize bridge and assign roles (5-15 min)
   - IL opens bridge; tags owner on service and storage components.
   - Bridge Operator posts initial status: "Investigating — impact, affected regions, ETA for next update".
3) Contain (15-45 min)
   - Apply safe mitigations: scale up reserved pools, add read-only fallbacks, route traffic to alternate region/model variant.
   - If mitigation has service-level risk, IL must log decision & reason in bridge notes.
4) Stabilize (45 min — 4 hrs)
   - Confirm traffic and SLO trends returning to baseline.
   - Create short-term change (e.g., config toggles) with the SRE guardrail checklist.
5) Restore & validate (4 hrs — 24 hrs)
   - Run smoke tests and customer-impact tests. Confirm no regressions.
   - If customer-affecting, Customer Success Liaison prepares account-specific notes.
6) Close & postmortem (24 hrs — 7 days)
   - Postmortem drafted within 48 hours; final review and action items tracked in the oncall board.

Triage checklist (copyable):
- Acknowledge pager
- Snapshot metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, 5xx counts)
- Check autoscale and GPU pool health (node counts, GPU OOM logs)
- Query routing & traffic split (region, model variant)
- Identify any recent deploys or config changes
- Enable throttling/unassign noisy tenants if necessary

Runbook template (canonical) — paste into service runbooks and keep small:
- Title: <service-name> incident runbook
- Symptoms: <short list>
- Initial checks (commands):
  - curl -i https://svc.internal/health || echo "service down"
  - kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=<svc> --no-headers
  - rrdtool fetch /metrics/requests "LAST"
- Quick mitigations (ordered):
  1) Redirect traffic to healthy region: routerctl route set <svc> --region us-west-2
  2) Scale dedicated pool: redwoodctl pool scale --name dedicated-<svc> --replicas +2
  3) Toggle prefix cache bypass: redwoodctl cache update --service <svc> --mode bypass
- Escalation: if not resolved in 30 min escalate to service owner and SRE lead
- Post-incident tasks: add telemetry, add synthetic checks, schedule canary test

Operational guardrails and safe-change checklist (for oncall change approvals):
- Has the change been reviewed by the IL? (Y/N)
- Does this change risk customer data loss? (Y/N)
- Will the change roll back automatically if error rate increases? (Y/N)
- Is there a scheduled quiet window? (Y/N)
- Notify Customer Success if >10 customers affected.

On-call rotation design patterns (recommended):
- Primary/secondary weekly cadence: Primary is the responder for the week; secondary takes over bridge ops and after-hours mitigation approval.
- Follow-the-sun overlap windows: 0700–1000 PST and 1500–1800 PST to cross-handover knowledge.
- Two-week shadow apprenticeship for new oncall engineers with graded responsibilities.
- Rotation docs should include runbook links, oncall-level decision ladders, and a small playbook index.

Game day blueprint (90–120 min session):
- Objective: validate cross-region failover, KV cache warmup, and backup routing to model-variant fallbacks.
- Participants: SREs (2), service owners (2), Customer Success (1), Observability engineer (1).
- Pre-reqs: baseline synthetic pass, canary traffic generator configured, and a standby customer liaison.
- Exercise steps:
  1) Trigger simulated GPU pool OOM in us-east-1 (execution by infra engineer).
  2) Observe autoscaler response and confirm traffic spill to us-west-2.
  3) Validate prefix cache warmup in target region and measure p95 delta.
  4) Test customer comm template and time-to-first-notice.
- Scoring: time-to-bridge <=5 min, time-to-first-mitigation <=20 min, p95 recovery to within 2x baseline within 30 min.

Status page and customer communication templates
- Principles: be fast, factual, and actionable. Avoid speculation; give an ETA for next update. Use the phrase "investigating" until mitigation verified.

Template A — Initial public status (short):
Title: Degraded performance affecting inference endpoints\Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or errors.\Current status: Investigating — we are seeing elevated error rates for traffic routed to us-east-1 queues.\Next update: in 30 minutes.
Advice for customers: If you use region pinned hosts, consider switching to us-west-2 as a temporary workaround. Contact support@redwood.ai for account-specific assistance.

Template B — Account-specific email (when known impact):
\Subject: Redwood status update — temporary performance degradation for <customer-name>\Hi <CS Rep> / <Customer Contact>,\We are investigating elevated error rates affecting requests for your account. Our engineers have applied a routing mitigation and are monitoring.\What we’re doing: scaled dedicated pool for your tenant and moved traffic to encrypted-us-west-2 nodes.\Action for you: no action required unless you continue to see errors. If you prefer, we can coordinate a manual failover at a scheduled time.\Estimated next update: <ETA>

Template C — Post-incident customer closing note and remediation offer:
\Subject: Incident resolved — summary and remediation options for <customer-name>\Hi <Customer Contact>,\Summary: On <date> we experienced a performance degradation caused by <root-cause>. The service was fully restored at <time>.\Impact: Your account experienced ~X% additional latency and Y failed requests during the incident window.\What we fixed: <short list of technical remediations>.\Compensation: We will credit <X>% of the affected usage billed in <month> per our SLA. Please let your CS rep know if you require additional evidence.\Next steps: we scheduled a targeted follow-up with your team to discuss longer-term mitigations.\nRegards,\Customer Success / Incident Response

Postmortem template (required fields):
- Title
- Incident ID
- Severity
- Start / End times (UTC)
- Affected services and customers
- Detecting signal(s)
- Root cause (one-paragraph)
- Timeline of events (minute-level bullets)
- Mitigations applied (short list)
- Corrective action(s) and owners (include ETA)
- Follow-up validations and telemetry to add
- Blameless summary and learnings

Example timeline excerpt (format):
- 2026-02-10T14:03Z — Pager triggered: router p95 > 1500ms
- 2026-02-10T14:05Z — Bridge opened; IL assigned: @marisol. Initial post to status page.
- 2026-02-10T14:16Z — Scale-up of dedicated pool in us-west-2 completed.
- 2026-02-10T14:42Z — p95 returned to baseline; monitoring stable.

SLOs and evidence collection (minimum):
- SLOs to monitor: request p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, queue depth, and head-of-line latency.
- Evidence archive: bridge log (transcript), snapshots of dashboards, relevant kube logs (kubectl logs with timestamps), and saved tracer spans (jaeger link).
- Retention: put incident evidence into the incident-bucket with path: s3://incident-evidence/<incident-id>/ and tag the runbook entry.

Escalation matrix (short bullets):

Content: Summary:
This document collates the core incident lifecycle guidance, runbook templates, on-call rotation patterns, game-day play outlines, and customer-facing status templates we use to fulfill commitments when Redwood experiences service disruptions. It is intended for SREs, service owners, customer success, and on-call engineers.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: Applies to all public-facing inference endpoints (hosted API, dedicated pools) and control-plane services that impact customer request routing, billing, or data access.
- Intent: Reduce time-to-stabilize, make customer communication predictable and clear, and ensure post-incident learning drives improvements to SLOs and runbooks.

Quick reference: roles and responsibilities
1) Incident Lead (IL) — generally the oncall SRE or service owner. Owns timeline, decisions, and customer brief cadence.
2) Bridge Operator — runs the war-room (Zoom/MS Teams), snapshots evidence, posts updates to the status page.
3) Tier-1 Responder — initial triage, short-term mitigations, tooling to mute noisy alerts.
4) Tier-2/3 Engineers — deep debugging, remediation, and config changes.
5) Customer Success Liaison — crafts external messaging and liaises with affected accounts.
6) Postmortem Owner — writes the retrospective, tracks action items.

Incident classification matrix (short):

Incident lifecycle (detailed run-loop):
1) Detection & initial triage (0-5 min)
   - Pager fires; Tier-1 responder acknowledges in 5 min.
   - Collect these 3 data points within first 10 minutes: symptom (error/latency), blast radius (tenants/regions), and possible choke points (GPU pool, autoscaler, network).
2) Mobilize bridge and assign roles (5-15 min)
   - IL opens bridge; tags owner on service and storage components.
   - Bridge Operator posts initial status: "Investigating — impact, affected regions, ETA for next update".
3) Contain (15-45 min)
   - Apply safe mitigations: scale up reserved pools, add read-only fallbacks, route traffic to alternate region/model variant.
   - If mitigation has service-level risk, IL must log decision & reason in bridge notes.
4) Stabilize (45 min — 4 hrs)
   - Confirm traffic and SLO trends returning to baseline.
   - Create short-term change (e.g., config toggles) with the SRE guardrail checklist.
5) Restore & validate (4 hrs — 24 hrs)
   - Run smoke tests and customer-impact tests. Confirm no regressions.
   - If customer-affecting, Customer Success Liaison prepares account-specific notes.
6) Close & postmortem (24 hrs — 7 days)
   - Postmortem drafted within 48 hours; final review and action items tracked in the oncall board.

- Objective: validate cross-region failover, KV cache warmup, and backup routing to model-variant fallbacks.

This ticket consolidates learnings from the Mar 2026 cross-region incident, implements immediate bugfixes and durable mitigations, and codifies playbooks for operators to safely route traffic between regions (including model-variant fallbacks and cache-warmup strategies).\",\n  \"incident_summary\": \"On 2026-03-08 we observed correlated p95 latency spikes and request errors originating in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 across both hosted and dedicated deployments. Primary cause was a kernel selection regression combined with KV cache eviction behavior after autoscaler churn on dedicated GPU pools. Impact: degraded responses for ~40% of hosted requests to affected regions and reduced throughput for 3 dedicated customers. Several customers escalated to SEs and SREs during the incident.\",\n  \"mitigation_actions\": [\n    \"2026-03-08 03:12 UTC: Eng oncall forced smart-routing policy to prefer eu-central-1 for affected routes (manual override) to reduce p95 latency\",\n    \"2026-03-08 03:25 UTC: Increased dedicated pool capacity (reserve burst nodes) for two impacted customers to prevent ongoing OOMs\",\n    \"2026-03-08 03:40 UTC: Rolled back the recent kernel optimization flag on runtime nodes in us-west-2 (reverted build r-infer-1.18.3) which stopped new OOM patterns\",\n    \"2026-03-08 04:05 UTC: Warmed KV caches in the target region by replaying recent popular prefixes via the cache-warm endpoint and a targeted batch job\",\n    \"2026-03-08 04:30 UTC: Updated customer-facing status page and proactive SE outreach for top 10 affected customers\"\n  ],\n  \"proposed_runbook\": [\n    \"Phase 0 - Detection: Confirm cross-region scope using global latency dashboard, p95/p99 error heatmap, and dedicated pool telemetry (GPU OOMs, scheduling failures). Use tag 'cross-region' in the incident room.\",\n    \"Phase 1 - Containment: If two or more regions show sustained p95 > 2x baseline AND error rate increase > 3x, initiate cross-region failover protocol.\",\n    \"Phase 2 - Traffic Shift Preparation: Verify capacity in candidate target region (available GPU slots, model variant compatibility, matching quantization profiles). Check KV cache hit rate history and plan for warmup time (estimate warmup RTT per prefix).\",\n    \"Phase 3 - Traffic Shift Execution (manual steps):\",\n    \"  1) Enter maintenance window in Console for affected routes and pause background billing-heavy tasks for dedicated customers as needed.\",\n    \"  2) Adjust Smart Routing weights: set primary region weight to 0.1 and target region to 0.9 in increments (0 -> 10% -> 50% -> 90%) with 2 minute observation between steps.\",\n    \"  3) If using DNS-based mitigation, ensure global LB TTL <= 60s before initiating. Prefer global LB weight updates over DNS for lower lead time.\",\n    \"  4) Warm KV caches via /internal/cache-warm for top 200 prefixes and run a controlled synthetic load at 5-10% of production RPS to pre-fill caches.\",\n    \"  5) Validate functional correctness: run smoke tests (generation, chat, embeddings) against target region and compare outputs against golden prompts (allowing model-variant deltas).\",\n    \"Phase 4 - Post-shift Validation: Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and client-side observed timeouts for 30 minutes at steady traffic. Ensure SLOs return to acceptable thresholds. If regression observed, revert weights by 50% or fall back to canary route.\",\n    \"Phase 5 - Rollback Criteria: Define automatic rollback triggers: sustained >15% error rate increase, p99 > 3x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes, or CPU/GPU OOMs on >3 nodes in the target region.\",\n    \"Phase 6 - Communication: Standardized templates for status page, customer emails, and internal incident notes. Include expected ETA for final switchover or rollback and list of affected deployments.\",\n    \"Automations to implement: 'rctl shift-traffic --from us-west-2 --to eu-central-1 --percent 50 --step 10 --wait 120s' with dry-run mode and automated pre-checks. Add a 'dry-fallback' flag to immediately rehydrate previous routing on failure triggers.\"\n  ],\n  \"changes_and_PRs\": [\n    \"GH: redwood-inference/runtime#5421 - Revert kernel selection heuristic change and add feature flag gating for future kernel experiments\",\n    \"GH: redwood-console/ops#331 - Smart-routing weight change API with validation and dry-run support\",\n    \"GH: redwood-infra/automation#188 - rctl traffic-shift automation prototype and canary harness\",\n    \"Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Cross-Region+Failover+Runbook (draft)\"\n  ],\n  \"follow_up_tasks\": [\n    \"Add unit and e2e tests for kernel selection heuristic (ENG-4840)\",\n    \"Ship smart-routing dry-run and pre-checks (ENG-4872)\",\n    \"Implement KV cache telemetry to surface warmup progress to Console (PM-412)\",\n    \"Validate Dedicated autoscaler behavior under rolling updates and add protective cool-down (ENG-4899)\",\n    \"Schedule tabletop run with SEs + SREs to walk the runbook (completed by 2026-03-18)\",\n    \"Prepare customer-facing FAQ and postmortem (PM + Support collaboration)\",\n    \"Create synthetic workload for cache-warm smoke tests and include in nightly upgrade jobs\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"related_issues\": [\n    \"ENG-4700\",\n    \"ENG-4840\",\n    \"ENG-4872\",\n    \"PM-412\"\n  ],\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"https://monitoring.redwood.ai/dashboards/global-latency-heatmap?range=2026-03-08\",\n    \"https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-08-cross-region\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5421\",\n    \"https://drive.google.com/file/d/12MockRunbookDraft\"\n  ],\n  \"approvals\": [\n    \"SRE Lead -       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Orchestrated cross-region failover & traffic-shift runbook for hosted + dedicated\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-orchestrated-region-failover-runbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: reliability-failover-2026\nTeam: engineering\n\n# Orchestrated cross-region failover & traffic-shift runbook for hosted + dedicated\n\nKey: ENG-4821\n\nTeam: engineering\n\nTitle: Orchestrated cross-region failover & traffic-shift runbook for hosted + dedicated\n\nStatus: In Progress\n\nPriority: P0\n\nCreated At: 2026-03-10\n\nUpdated At: 2026-03-14\n\nCreator: Maya Patel\n\nAssignee: Liam Chen\n\nProject: reliability-failover-2026\n\nCycle: 2026-W11\n\nEstimate: 8\n\nDue Date: 2026-03-20\n\n## Labels\n\n- incident-response\n  - runbook\n  - hosted\n  - dedicated\n  - cross-region\n  - oncall\n  - postmortem-needed\n\nDescription: Create a validated, tested runbook and automation for cross-region outages and controlled traffic shifting that covers both Redwood Hosted API and Dedicated capacity customers. This ticket consolidates learnings from the Mar 2026 cross-region incident, implements immediate bugfixes and durable mitigations, and codifies playbooks for operators to safely route traffic between regions (including model-variant fallbacks and cache-warmup strategies).\n\nIncident Summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed correlated p95 latency spikes and request errors originating in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 across both hosted and dedicated deployments. Primary cause was a kernel selection regression combined with KV cache eviction behavior after autoscaler churn on dedicated GPU pools. Impact: degraded responses for ~40% of hosted requests to affected regions and reduced throughput for 3 dedicated customers. Several customers escalated to SEs and SREs during the incident.\n\n## Mitigation Actions",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Orchestrated cross-region failover & traffic-shift runbook for hosted + dedicated\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-orchestrated-region-failover-runbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: reliability-failover-2026\nTeam: engineering\n\nPrimary cause was a kernel selection regression combined with KV cache eviction behavior after autoscaler churn on dedicated GPU pools. Impact: degraded responses for ~40% of hosted requests to affected regions and reduced throughput for 3 dedicated customers. Several customers escalated to SEs and SREs during the incident.\n\n## Mitigation Actions\n\n- 2026-03-08 03:12 UTC: Eng oncall forced smart-routing policy to prefer eu-central-1 for affected routes (manual override) to reduce p95 latency\n  - 2026-03-08 03:25 UTC: Increased dedicated pool capacity (reserve burst nodes) for two impacted customers to prevent ongoing OOMs\n  - 2026-03-08 03:40 UTC: Rolled back the recent kernel optimization flag on runtime nodes in us-west-2 (reverted build r-infer-1.18.3) which stopped new OOM patterns\n  - 2026-03-08 04:05 UTC: Warmed KV caches in the target region by replaying recent popular prefixes via the cache-warm endpoint and a targeted batch job\n  - 2026-03-08 04:30 UTC: Updated customer-facing status page and proactive SE outreach for top 10 affected customers\n\n## Proposed Runbook",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Orchestrated cross-region failover & traffic-shift runbook for hosted + dedicated\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-4821-orchestrated-region-failover-runbook.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: reliability-failover-2026\nTeam: engineering\n\n- Phase 0 - Detection: Confirm cross-region scope using global latency dashboard, p95/p99 error heatmap, and dedicated pool telemetry (GPU OOMs, scheduling failures). Use tag 'cross-region' in the incident room.\n  - Phase 1 - Containment: If two or more regions show sustained p95 > 2x baseline AND error rate increase > 3x, initiate cross-region failover protocol.\n  - Phase 2 - Traffic Shift Preparation: Verify capacity in candidate target region (available GPU slots, model variant compatibility, matching quantization profiles). Check KV cache hit rate history and plan for warmup time (estimate warmup RTT per prefix).\n  - Phase 3 - Traffic Shift Execution (manual steps):\n  -   1) Enter maintenance window in Console for affected routes and pause background billing-heavy tasks for dedicated customers as needed.\n  -   2) Adjust Smart Routing weights: set primary region weight to 0.1 and target region to 0.9 in increments (0 -> 10% -> 50% -> 90%) with 2 minute observation between steps.\n  -   3) If using DNS-based mitigation, ensure global LB TTL <= 60s before initiating. Prefer global LB weight updates over DNS for lower lead time.\n  -   4) Warm KV caches via /internal/cache-warm for top 200 prefixes and run a controlled synthetic load at 5-10% of production RPS to pre-fill caches.\n  -   5) Validate functional correctness: run smoke tests (generation, chat, embeddings) against target region and compare outputs against golden prompts (allowing model-variant deltas).\n  - Phase 4 - Post-shift Validation: Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and client-side observed timeouts for 30 minutes at steady traffic. Ensure SLOs return to acceptable thresholds. If regression observed, revert weights by 50% or fall back to canary route.\n  - Phase 5 - Rollback Criteria: Define automatic rollback triggers: sustained >15% error rate increase, p99 > 3x baseline",

  "description": "Create a validated, tested runbook and automation for cross-region outages and controlled traffic shifting that covers both Redwood Hosted API and Dedicated capacity customers. This ticket consolidates learnings from the Mar 2026 cross-region incident, implements immediate bugfixes and durable mitigations, and codifies playbooks for operators to safely route traffic between regions (including model-variant fallbacks and cache-warmup strategies).",
  "incident_summary": "On 2026-03-08 we observed correlated p95 latency spikes and request errors originating in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 across both hosted and dedicated deployments. Primary cause was a kernel selection regression combined with KV cache eviction behavior after autoscaler churn on dedicated GPU pools. Impact: degraded responses for ~40% of hosted requests to affected regions and reduced throughput for 3 dedicated customers. Several customers escalated to SEs and SREs during the incident.",
  "mitigation_actions": [
    "2026-03-08 03:12 UTC: Eng oncall forced smart-routing policy to prefer eu-central-1 for affected routes (manual override) to reduce p95 latency",
    "2026-03-08 03:25 UTC: Increased dedicated pool capacity (reserve burst nodes) for two impacted customers to prevent ongoing OOMs",
    "2026-03-08 03:40 UTC: Rolled back the recent kernel optimization flag on runtime nodes in us-west-2 (reverted build r-infer-1.18.3) which stopped new OOM patterns",
    "2026-03-08 04:05 UTC: Warmed KV caches in the target region by replaying recent popular prefixes via the cache-warm endpoint and a targeted batch job",
    "2026-03-08 04:30 UTC: Updated customer-facing status page and proactive SE outreach for top 10 affected customers"
  ],
  "proposed_runbook": [
    "Phase 0 - Detection: Confirm cross-region scope using global latency dashboard, p95/p99 error heatmap, and dedicated pool telemetry (GPU OOMs, scheduling failures). Use tag 'cross-region' in the incident room.",
    "Phase 1 - Containment: If two or more regions show sustained p95 > 2x baseline AND error rate increase > 3x, initiate cross-region failover protocol.",
    "Phase 2 - Traffic Shift Preparation: Verify capacity in candidate target region (available GPU slots, model variant compatibility, matching quantization profiles). Check KV cache hit rate history and plan for warmup time (estimate warmup RTT per prefix).",
    "Phase 3 - Traffic Shift Execution (manual steps):",
    "  1) Enter maintenance window in Console for affected routes and pause background billing-heavy tasks for dedicated customers as needed.",
    "  2) Adjust Smart Routing weights: set primary region weight to 0.1 and target region to 0.9 in increments (0 -> 10% -> 50% -> 90%) with 2 minute observation between steps.",
    "  3) If using DNS-based mitigation, ensure global LB TTL <= 60s before initiating. Prefer global LB weight updates over DNS for lower lead time.",
    "  4) Warm KV caches via /internal/cache-warm for top 200 prefixes and run a controlled synthetic load at 5-10% of production RPS to pre-fill caches.",
    "  5) Validate functional correctness: run smoke tests (generation, chat, embeddings) against target region and compare outputs against golden prompts (allowing model-variant deltas).",
    "Phase 4 - Post-shift Validation: Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and client-side observed timeouts for 30 minutes at steady traffic. Ensure SLOs return to acceptable thresholds. If regression observed, revert weights by 50% or fall back to canary route.",
    "Phase 5 - Rollback Criteria: Define automatic rollback triggers: sustained >15% error rate increase, p99 > 3x baseline for 10 consecutive minutes, or CPU/GPU OOMs on >3 nodes in the target region.",
    "Phase 6 - Communication: Standardized templates for status page, customer emails, and internal incident notes. Include expected ETA for final switchover or rollback and list of affected deployments.",
    "Automations to implement: 'rctl shift-traffic --from us-west-2 --to eu-central-1 --percent 50 --step 10 --wait 120s' with dry-run mode and automated pre-checks. Add a 'dry-fallback' flag to immediately rehydrate previous routing on failure triggers."
  ],

    "GH: redwood-console/ops#331 - Smart-routing weight change API with validation and dry-run support",
    "GH: redwood-infra/automation#188 - rctl traffic-shift automation prototype and canary harness",
    "Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Cross-Region+Failover+Runbook (draft)"
  ],
  "follow_up_tasks": [
    "Add unit and e2e tests for kernel selection heuristic (ENG-4840)",
    "Ship smart-routing dry-run and pre-checks (ENG-4872)",
    "Implement KV cache telemetry to surface warmup progress to Console (PM-412)",
    "Validate Dedicated autoscaler behavior under rolling updates and add protective cool-down (ENG-4899)",
    "Schedule tabletop run with SEs + SREs to walk the runbook (completed by 2026-03-18)",
    "Prepare customer-facing FAQ and postmortem (PM + Support collaboration)",

Description: Create a validated, tested runbook and automation for cross-region outages and controlled traffic shifting that covers both Redwood Hosted API and Dedicated capacity customers. This ticket consolidates learnings from the Mar 2026 cross-region incident, implements immediate bugfixes and durable mitigations, and codifies playbooks for operators to safely route traffic between regions (including model-variant fallbacks and cache-warmup strategies).

Incident Summary: On 2026-03-08 we observed correlated p95 latency spikes and request errors originating in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 across both hosted and dedicated deployments. Primary cause was a kernel selection regression combined with KV cache eviction behavior after autoscaler churn on dedicated GPU pools. Impact: degraded responses for ~40% of hosted requests to affected regions and reduced throughput for 3 dedicated customers. Several customers escalated to SEs and SREs during the incident.

## Mitigation Actions

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-30145\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-20\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"creator\": \"Aisha Kumar\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Miguel Santos\",\n  \"project\": \"release-core\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-W10\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-25\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"release-engineering\",\n    \"rollouts\",\n    \"safety\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"auto-rollback\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Goal: Build a reusable staged-release safety harness that combines lightweight canaries, percent-based traffic ramps, feature-flag gates, synthetic traffic checks, and automated rollback actions. This harness should be pluggable into Redwood's runtime and Console, support both Hosted and Dedicated deployments, and be compatible with Private (VPC) rollouts. The design must allow per-route and per-model policies, expose a clear audit trail, and provide measurable SLO-based pass/fail signals for automated decisions.\\n\\nDeliverables: a feature-flag controller API, a traffic-ramp controller integrated with the routing layer, a small state machine service for gate evaluations, predefined gate templates (latency/error/quality/regression), Console UI hooks for visualization, runbook + playbook for manual override, and a demo rollout on an internal non-prod model serving path.\",\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": \"1) Canary flow can be started from Console or API and will route 1% of traffic to the new version within 5 minutes.\\n2) System evaluates gates (p95 latency, 5xx rate, decode-error rate, and quality regression against golden prompts) and emits pass/fail decisions to Console timeline.\\n3) When any gate fails above configured threshold, the controller executes a rollback action within 30s and records the reason in audit logs.\\n4) Operators can override automation via Console, pausing or accelerating ramps.\\n5) Integration tests simulate synthetic traffic and verify auto-rollback triggers for injected faults.\\n6) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console.\",\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"Phase A (design & proto, 2 sprints): API and controller prototype; gate templates; unit tests.\\nPhase B (integration, 2 sprints): integrate with routing layer, Console UI, and metrics pipeline; end-to-end smoke tests.\\nPhase C (canary on internal model, 1 sprint): run 2 internal rollouts, validate thresholds, observe false-positive rate.\\nPhase D (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.\\nCanary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).\",\n  \"gates\": \"We will provide a set of preconfigured gates and allow custom metric expressions:\\n- Latency Gate: p95 increase <= 15% relative to baseline over gate window (default 15m).\\n- Error Gate: request 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (sliding 15m).\\n- Decode Failure Gate: any spike > 3x baseline triggers immediate fail.\\n- Quality Gate: evaluated by running 200 golden prompts against new and baseline models and checking BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta; fail if quality drops > configured delta (default 2%).\\n- Resource Gate: GPU memory pressure > 80% sustained for 5m causes pause.\\nGate evaluation semantics: each gate returns pass/warn/fail. A single fail triggers auto-rollback when automation is enabled. Warns pause ramp and require manual approval to continue.\",\n  \"instrumentation\": \"Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, 5xx counts, decode-fail counts, throughput, GPU memory/SM utilization.\\nTracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.\\nLogs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.\\nSynthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.\\nDashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.\\nPRs and contracts: routing-api PR (github.com/redwood/re-routing/pulls/212), controller proto (github.com/redwood/re-release/pulls/37).\",\n  \"risks_and_mitigation\": \"Risk: Overly aggressive auto-rollback causing noisy rollbacks for transient spikes. Mitigation: use smoothing windows, require sustained failure for X samples or use majority of gates failing rather than single noisy metric.\\nRisk: Quality gate adds cost/time. Mitigation: sample fewer golden prompts for fast gates and run full quality suite during longer wait windows.\\nRisk: Stateful migrations, backward-incompatible cache formats. Mitigation: short-circuit routing to warm KV caches and run data-migration job in parallel; document supported migration patterns for LTS channels.\\nRisk: Console automation dependency creates blast radius. Mitigation: default automation OFF for new customers; require opt-in and RBAC for manual overrides.\",\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-28990\",\n    \"ENG-27355\"\n  ],\n  \"parent_issue\": [\n    \"ENG-29801\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RELEASE-HARNESS-2026\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood/re-release/pull/37\",\n    \"https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rollouts/internal-canary-demo\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": \"2026-02-22: Initial design review with PMs \\u2014 agreed on quality gate approach; asked to reduce default golden prompt set.\\n2026-02-28: Security reviewed data flow; confirmed no user PII is sent to synthetic harness.\\n2026-03-04: Miguel pushed controller skeleton PR; awaiting test harness for golden prompt runner. PR: https://github.com/redwood/re-release/pull/42\\n2026-03-10: Ran internal canary against small classification model; observed latency spike at 5% ramp due to cold KV cache - added warmup hook.\\n2026-03-12: UX mockups for Console timeline uploaded; PM requested clearer manual-override CTA and audit export.\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"release\": \"runtime-2.4\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"false\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"acceptance_criteria\",\n    \"rollout_plan\",\n    \"gates\",\n    \"instrumentation\",\n    \"risks_and_mitigation\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_c301739e75014769b0c41047a9e91f96\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-30145-staged-safety-harness-and-dynamic-rollback.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: release-core\nTeam: engineering\n\n# Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback\n\nKey: ENG-30145\n\nTeam: engineering\n\nTitle: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback\n\nStatus: In Progress\n\nPriority: P1\n\nCreated At: 2026-02-20\n\nUpdated At: 2026-03-12\n\nCreator: Aisha Kumar\n\nAssignee: Miguel Santos\n\nProject: release-core\n\nCycle: 2026-W10\n\nEstimate: 5\n\nDue Date: 2026-03-25\n\n## Labels\n\n- release-engineering\n  - rollouts\n  - safety\n  - canary\n  - auto-rollback\n\nDescription: Goal: Build a reusable staged-release safety harness that combines lightweight canaries, percent-based traffic ramps, feature-flag gates, synthetic traffic checks, and automated rollback actions. This harness should be pluggable into Redwood's runtime and Console, support both Hosted and Dedicated deployments, and be compatible with Private (VPC) rollouts. The design must allow per-route and per-model policies, expose a clear audit trail, and provide measurable SLO-based pass/fail signals for automated decisions.\n\nDeliverables: a feature-flag controller API, a traffic-ramp controller integrated with the routing layer, a small state machine service for gate evaluations, predefined gate templates (latency/error/quality/regression), Console UI hooks for visualization, runbook + playbook for manual override, and a demo rollout on an internal non-prod model serving path.",

      "ordinal": 1,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-30145-staged-safety-harness-and-dynamic-rollback.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: release-core\nTeam: engineering\n\n-flag controller API, a traffic-ramp controller integrated with the routing layer, a small state machine service for gate evaluations, predefined gate templates (latency/error/quality/regression), Console UI hooks for visualization, runbook + playbook for manual override, and a demo rollout on an internal non-prod model serving path.\n\nAcceptance Criteria: 1) Canary flow can be started from Console or API and will route 1% of traffic to the new version within 5 minutes.\n2) System evaluates gates (p95 latency, 5xx rate, decode-error rate, and quality regression against golden prompts) and emits pass/fail decisions to Console timeline.\n3) When any gate fails above configured threshold, the controller executes a rollback action within 30s and records the reason in audit logs.\n4) Operators can override automation via Console, pausing or accelerating ramps.\n5) Integration tests simulate synthetic traffic and verify auto-rollback triggers for injected faults.\n6) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console.\n\nRollout Plan: Phase A (design & proto, 2 sprints): API and controller prototype; gate templates; unit tests.\nPhase B (integration, 2 sprints): integrate with routing layer, Console UI, and metrics pipeline; end-to-end smoke tests.\nPhase C (canary on internal model, 1 sprint): run 2 internal rollouts, validate thresholds, observe false-positive rate.\nPhase D (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.\nCanary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).",

      "ordinal": 2,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-30145-staged-safety-harness-and-dynamic-rollback.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: release-core\nTeam: engineering\n\nD (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.\nCanary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).\n\nGates: We will provide a set of preconfigured gates and allow custom metric expressions:\n- Latency Gate: p95 increase <= 15% relative to baseline over gate window (default 15m).\n- Error Gate: request 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (sliding 15m).\n- Decode Failure Gate: any spike > 3x baseline triggers immediate fail.\n- Quality Gate: evaluated by running 200 golden prompts against new and baseline models and checking BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta; fail if quality drops > configured delta (default 2%).\n- Resource Gate: GPU memory pressure > 80% sustained for 5m causes pause.\nGate evaluation semantics: each gate returns pass/warn/fail. A single fail triggers auto-rollback when automation is enabled. Warns pause ramp and require manual approval to continue.\n\nInstrumentation: Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, 5xx counts, decode-fail counts, throughput, GPU memory/SM utilization.\nTracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.\nLogs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.\nSynthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.\nDashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.\nPRs and contracts: routing-api PR (github.com/redwood/re-routing/pulls/212), controller proto (github.com/redwood/re-release/pulls/37).",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-30145-staged-safety-harness-and-dynamic-rollback.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: release-core\nTeam: engineering\n\nhits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.\nDashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.\nPRs and contracts: routing-api PR (github.com/redwood/re-routing/pulls/212), controller proto (github.com/redwood/re-release/pulls/37).\n\nRisks And Mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive auto-rollback causing noisy rollbacks for transient spikes. Mitigation: use smoothing windows, require sustained failure for X samples or use majority of gates failing rather than single noisy metric.\nRisk: Quality gate adds cost/time. Mitigation: sample fewer golden prompts for fast gates and run full quality suite during longer wait windows.\nRisk: Stateful migrations, backward-incompatible cache formats. Mitigation: short-circuit routing to warm KV caches and run data-migration job in parallel; document supported migration patterns for LTS channels.\nRisk: Console automation dependency creates blast radius. Mitigation: default automation OFF for new customers; require opt-in and RBAC for manual overrides.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- ENG-28990\n  - ENG-27355\n\n## Parent Issue\n\n- ENG-29801\n\n## Links\n\n- https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/RELEASE-HARNESS-2026\n  - https://github.com/redwood/re-release/pull/37\n  - https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rollouts/internal-canary-demo",

# Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback

Key: ENG-30145

Team: engineering

Title: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback

Status: In Progress

Priority: P1

Created At: 2026-02-20

Updated At: 2026-03-12

Creator: Aisha Kumar

Assignee: Miguel Santos

Project: release-core

Cycle: 2026-W10

Estimate: 5

Due Date: 2026-03-25

## Labels

- release-engineering
  - rollouts
  - safety
  - canary
  - auto-rollback

Description: Goal: Build a reusable staged-release safety harness that combines lightweight canaries, percent-based traffic ramps, feature-flag gates, synthetic traffic checks, and automated rollback actions. This harness should be pluggable into Redwood's runtime and Console, support both Hosted and Dedicated deployments, and be compatible with Private (VPC) rollouts. The design must allow per-route and per-model policies, expose a clear audit trail, and provide measurable SLO-based pass/fail signals for automated decisions.

Deliverables: a feature-flag controller API, a traffic-ramp controller integrated with the routing layer, a small state machine service for gate evaluations, predefined gate templates (latency/error/quality/regression), Console UI hooks for visualization, runbook + playbook for manual override, and a demo rollout on an internal non-prod model serving path.

[Document context]
Title: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback
Source: EnterpriseRAG/linear
Path: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-30145-staged-safety-harness-and-dynamic-rollback.json
Connector: linear
Workspace: engineering
Project: release-core
Team: engineering

-flag controller API, a traffic-ramp controller integrated with the routing layer, a small state machine service for gate evaluations, predefined gate templates (latency/error/quality/regression), Console UI hooks for visualization, runbook + playbook for manual override, and a demo rollout on an internal non-prod model serving path.

Acceptance Criteria: 1) Canary flow can be started from Console or API and will route 1% of traffic to the new version within 5 minutes.
2) System evaluates gates (p95 latency, 5xx rate, decode-error rate, and quality regression against golden prompts) and emits pass/fail decisions to Console timeline.
3) When any gate fails above configured threshold, the controller executes a rollback action within 30s and records the reason in audit logs.
4) Operators can override automation via Console, pausing or accelerating ramps.
5) Integration tests simulate synthetic traffic and verify auto-rollback triggers for injected faults.
6) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console.

Rollout Plan: Phase A (design & proto, 2 sprints): API and controller prototype; gate templates; unit tests.
Phase B (integration, 2 sprints): integrate with routing layer, Console UI, and metrics pipeline; end-to-end smoke tests.
Phase C (canary on internal model, 1 sprint): run 2 internal rollouts, validate thresholds, observe false-positive rate.
Phase D (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.
Canary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).

[Document context]
Title: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback
Source: EnterpriseRAG/linear
Path: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-30145-staged-safety-harness-and-dynamic-rollback.json
Connector: linear
Workspace: engineering
Project: release-core
Team: engineering

D (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.
Canary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).

Gates: We will provide a set of preconfigured gates and allow custom metric expressions:
- Latency Gate: p95 increase <= 15% relative to baseline over gate window (default 15m).
- Error Gate: request 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (sliding 15m).
- Decode Failure Gate: any spike > 3x baseline triggers immediate fail.
- Quality Gate: evaluated by running 200 golden prompts against new and baseline models and checking BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta; fail if quality drops > configured delta (default 2%).
- Resource Gate: GPU memory pressure > 80% sustained for 5m causes pause.
Gate evaluation semantics: each gate returns pass/warn/fail. A single fail triggers auto-rollback when automation is enabled. Warns pause ramp and require manual approval to continue.

Instrumentation: Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, 5xx counts, decode-fail counts, throughput, GPU memory/SM utilization.
Tracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.
Logs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.
Synthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.
Dashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.
PRs and contracts: routing-api PR (github.com/redwood/re-routing/pulls/212), controller proto (github.com/redwood/re-release/pulls/37).

Title: Staged release safety harness with dynamic canaries and auto-rollback
Source: EnterpriseRAG/linear
Path: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-30145-staged-safety-harness-and-dynamic-rollback.json
Connector: linear
Workspace: engineering
Project: release-core

hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.
Dashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.
PRs and contracts: routing-api PR (github.com/redwood/re-routing/pulls/212), controller proto (github.com/redwood/re-release/pulls/37).

Risks And Mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive auto-rollback causing noisy rollbacks for transient spikes. Mitigation: use smoothing windows, require sustained failure for X samples or use majority of gates failing rather than single noisy metric.
Risk: Quality gate adds cost/time. Mitigation: sample fewer golden prompts for fast gates and run full quality suite during longer wait windows.
Risk: Stateful migrations, backward-incompatible cache formats. Mitigation: short-circuit routing to warm KV caches and run data-migration job in parallel; document supported migration patterns for LTS channels.
Risk: Console automation dependency creates blast radius. Mitigation: default automation OFF for new customers; require opt-in and RBAC for manual overrides.

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/gmail",
    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"gml-20260208-camila-0071\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"camila_reyes\",\n  \"subject\": \"Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"camila_reyes\",\n    \"karthik_iyer\",\n    \"marissa_cole\",\n    \"lauren_bishop\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>\",\n    \"Procurements <procurements@brightedge.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"6\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2026-02-08T09:12:00-08:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2026-02-11T15:48:00-07:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"procurement\",\n  \"related_account\": \"BrightEdge Analytics\",\n  \"deal_id\": \"BD-2026-0412\",\n  \"region\": \"us\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"Redwood-SLO-Measurement-Guide.pdf\",\n    \"BrightEdge-Procurement-Questionnaire.xlsx\",\n    \"SLO-Definitions.md\",\n    \"SOC2-report-redwood.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://console.redwood.com/projects/brightedge/metrics\",\n    \"https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Procurement/BrightEdge-SLO-answers\",\n    \"https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/exhibit-a\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>\\\\nTo: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>\\\\nCc: Procurements <procurements@brightedge.com>\\\\nDate: 2026-02-08 09:12 -0800\\\\nSubject: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\\\n\\\\nHi Elena \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nThanks for sending over the procurement packet. I've attached a short Redwood SLO Measurement Guide that summarizes how we define and measure uptime and latency for both Hosted and Dedicated customers. A few quick items we want to clarify from your questionnaire so we can populate the spreadsheet cleanly:\\\\n\\\\n- Measurement window: do you want monthly rolling windows or calendar-month snapshots? We typically report both but publish calendar-month for billing/SLAs and rolling 30-day for operational view.\\\\n- Latency percentiles: do you require p95 only, or p99/p999 for tail analysis? We can include standard buckets (p50/p90/p95/p99).\\\\n- Alerting expectations: do you need direct pager notifications for incidents or prefer webhook/ops channel integration?\\\\n- Customer access: we can provision read-only dashboards and metric exports; confirm whether you need raw trace access.\\\\n\\\\nIf you share the Excel questionnaire, I can route to engineering for precise definitions and provide example dashboard links. Happy to set up a 30-minute call with Karthik and Marissa if you'd like to walk line-by-line.\\\\n\\\\nBest,\\\\nCamila Reyes\\\\nDirector, Strategic Accounts\\\\nRedwood Inference\\\\n\\\\nAttachments: Redwood-SLO-Measurement-Guide.pdf\",\n    \"From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>\\\\nTo: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>\\\\nDate: 2026-02-08 10:03 -0800\\\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\\\n\\\\nHi Camila \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nThanks for the guide \\u2014 attaching our procurement questionnaire (BrightEdge-Procurement-Questionnaire.xlsx). A few items specifically called out by our SRE/procurement teams:\\\\n\\\\n1) We require SLA reporting at calendar-month granularity for billing and credits.\\\\n2) We need p99 and p95 for latency, plus mean and 99.9th when available.\\\\n3) A definition of \\\\\\\"availability\\\\\\\" you use (which errors count as downtime).\\\\n4) Access model: read-only dashboard link, metric export (CSV/Prometheus scrape), and whether we can configure alerts to hit our PagerDuty.\\\\n5) Retention: metrics/log retention windows and the export process for audits.\\\\n\\\\nCan your team confirm whether we can get a read-only dashboard URL and an example of the alert payload we would receive? If possible, please include a note on exception handling during maintenance windows and large-scale migrations.\\\\n\\\\nThanks \\u2014 Elena\\\\nElena Torres\\\\nHead of Procurement, BrightEdge\\\\n\\\\nAttachment: BrightEdge-Procurement-Questionnaire.xlsx\",\n    \"From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>\\\\nTo: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>\\\\nCc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com\\\\nDate: 2026-02-09 11:20 -0800\\\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\\\n\\\\nHi Elena \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nI pulled together the technical definitions requested and attached a short SLO-Definitions.md. High-level answers below (happy to expand line-by-line against the Excel):\\\\n\\\\n- Availability definition: We define a request as \\\\\\\"failed\\\\\\\" when the service returns any 5xx or when the request exceeds a hard timeout (default 30s). Network-level connection failures and closed TCP sessions are also counted as failures for availability SLOs. We exclude client-side timeouts attributable to client misconfiguration.\\\\n\\\\n- Measurement unit: Per-request evaluation aggregated to 1-minute buckets across the region(s) you use, then rolled up to calendar-month for SLA reporting. The reported uptime = 1 - (failed_requests / total_requests) over the chosen window.\\\\n\\\\n- Latency: We compute p50/p90/p95/p99 on end-to-end request latency (time from request ingress at our edge to final token emitted). For very short-lived requests we also report median and p99.9 on demand. Latency percentiles are computed on the same 1-minute buckets and then combined using weighted aggregation to preserve percentile characteristics.\\\\n\\\\n- Sampling: By default we measure 100% of production traffic for availability and latency percentiles. For extremely high-volume customers we provide a configurable sampling policy but only if requested; sampling policies are documented and applied consistently.\\\\n\\\\n- Synthetic checks: We run synthetic health probes every 30s across regions. Synthetic checks feed an independent availability signal used for platform-level alerts (not billing) and are included in incident reviews.\\\\n\\\\n- Error budget & exceptions: Error budgets are tracked on a rolling 30-day and calendar-month basis. For scheduled maintenance windows we offer two options: (1) pre-agreed maintenance windows that are exempt from SLA calculations if scheduled >72h in advance and posted to the status page; (2) emergency maintenance which we evaluate for credit eligibility after post-incident review. Non-Redwood third-party platform outages (e.g., cloud provider outages) are treated per the standard force-majeure section but we provide detailed logs for audits.\\\\n\\\\nAttachment: SLO-Definitions.md\\\\n\\\\nIf you want, I can produce an export of 3 months of sample metrics from our staging environment to show calculation mechanics.\\\\n\\\\n\\u2014Karthik\",\n    \"From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>\\\\nTo: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>\\\\nDate: 2026-02-10 08:45 -0800\\\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\\\n\\\\nElena \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nQuick note on observability and customer access:\\\\n\\\\n- Dashboards: Customers get a pre-built read-only Grafana dashboard (hosted inside the Redwood Console) that includes uptime, request rates, error rates, and latency percentiles. We can provision a console project with a single sign-on link that BrightEdge SREs can use; link included below.\\\\n- Metrics export: We support Prometheus remote write and periodic CSV exports for audited reporting. For large exports we can provide S3-delivered dumps.\\\\n- Alerts: Customers can create alerting rules in the Console and route incidents to PagerDuty, Slack, or webhook endpoints. We can also push our platform alerts to your PagerDuty on request (we provide template payloads).\\\\n- Traces/logs: Read-only access to traces is available with RBAC; full raw logs can be forwarded to your cloud storage or SIEM for retention.\\\\n- Compliance docs: SOC 2 report and recent penetration-test summary available; will attach SOC2-report-redwood.pdf to the final packet.\\\\n\\\\nConsole dashboard (read-only sample): https://console.redwood.com/projects/brightedge/metrics\\\\nDrive with example exports: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Procurement/BrightEdge-SLO-answers\\\\n\\\\nIf you prefer a walkthrough, I can demo the dashboard and show how a calendar-month SLA report is generated.\\\\n\\\\nThanks,\\\\nMarissa Cole\\\\nPlatform Reliability\\\\nRedwood Inference\",\n    \"From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>\\\\nTo: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>\\\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com\\\\nDate: 2026-02-11 14:02 -0700\\\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\\\n\\\\nElena \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nConsolidating the answers from engineering and reliability:\\\\n\\\\n1) SLA baseline: For Dedicated deployments our standard SLA is 99.95% monthly availability; for Hosted customers we publish a 99.9% baseline with higher tiers available by contract.\\\\n2) Measurement and reporting: Calendar-month for billing and SLA credits; rolling 30-day for operational dashboards. We will provide the CSV/Prometheus export for the months requested and a sample calculation workbook.\\\\n3) Alerts & access: We will provision a read-only console project with Grafana dashboards and an Ops webhook template for PagerDuty. If BrightEdge wants us to send platform alerts into your PD schedule, we can set that as part of the onboarding checklist.\\\\n4) Exceptions: Maintenance windows scheduled >72 hours in advance will be excluded from SLA calculations if agreed in writing. For unexpected platform events, we will run a post-incident review and recommend credit adjustments per the standard SLA exhibit; these are handled case-by-case.\\\\n\\\\nNext steps I propose:\\\\n- I will fill your Excel with the responses above and return it by EOD tomorrow.\\\\n- Schedule a 30-minute technical review \\u2014 Karthik and Marissa are available Wednesday (Feb 11) 10:00\\u201312:00 PT or Thursday 14:00\\u201316:00 PT.\\\\n- If procurement is ready, I can generate the Exhibit A (SLA) DocuSign and include the monitoring access checklist.\\\\n\\\\nLet me know which time works for your SREs and procurement.\\\\n\\\\nBest,\\\\nCamila\",\n    \"From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>\\\\nTo: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>\\\\nCc: Procurements <procurements@brightedge.com>\\\\nDate: 2026-02-11 15:48 -0700\\\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\\\n\\\\nHi Camila \\u2014\\\\n\\\\nThis is great, thank you. Please send the completed Excel and the Exhibit A DocuSign when ready. For the technical review, Thursday 14:00 PT works for our SREs.\\\\n\\\\nAlso request: sample 3-month calculation export for calendar months Dec/Jan/Feb so we can validate the math before signature. If you can stage the read-only dashboard earlier that would help our team run through the alerts.\\\\n\\\\nI'll loop in procurement to confirm contract language after we validate the numbers.\\\\n\\\\n\\u2014Elena\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_dbe82d0294f24d1c92e92ca24a5ee56b\"\n}",

A few items specifically called out by our SRE/procurement teams:\\n\\n1) We require SLA reporting at calendar-month granularity for billing and credits.\\n2) We need p99 and p95 for latency, plus mean and 99.9th when available.\\n3) A definition of \\\"availability\\\" you use (which errors count as downtime).\\n4) Access model: read-only dashboard link, metric export (CSV/Prometheus scrape), and whether we can configure alerts to hit our PagerDuty.\\n5) Retention: metrics/log retention windows and the export process for audits.\\n\\nCan your team confirm whether we can get a read-only dashboard URL and an example of the alert payload we would receive? If possible, please include a note on exception handling during maintenance windows and large-scale migrations.\\n\\nThanks — Elena\\nElena Torres\\nHead of Procurement, BrightEdge\\n\\nAttachment: BrightEdge-Procurement-Questionnaire.xlsx\n  - From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>\\nTo: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>\\nCc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com\\nDate: 2026-02-09 11:20 -0800\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\n\\nHi Elena —\\n\\nI pulled together the technical definitions requested and attached a short SLO-Definitions.md.       "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/gmail\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/camila_reyes/20260208-availability-metrics-questionnaire.json\nConnector: gmail\nWorkspace: camila_reyes\n\n):\\n\\n- Availability definition: We define a request as \\\"failed\\\" when the service returns any 5xx or when the request exceeds a hard timeout (default 30s). Network-level connection failures and closed TCP sessions are also counted as failures for availability SLOs. We exclude client-side timeouts attributable to client misconfiguration.\\n\\n- Measurement unit: Per-request evaluation aggregated to 1-minute buckets across the region(s) you use, then rolled up to calendar-month for SLA reporting. The reported uptime = 1 - (failed_requests / total_requests) over the chosen window.\\n\\n- Latency: We compute p50/p90/p95/p99 on end-to-end request latency (time from request ingress at our edge to final token emitted). For very short-lived requests we also report median and p99.9 on demand. Latency percentiles are computed on the same 1-minute buckets and then combined using weighted aggregation to preserve percentile characteristics.\\n\\n- Sampling: By default we measure 100% of production traffic for availability and latency percentiles. For extremely high-volume customers we provide a configurable sampling policy but only if requested; sampling policies are documented and applied consistently.\\n\\n- Synthetic checks: We run synthetic health probes every 30s across regions. Synthetic checks feed an independent availability signal used for platform-level alerts (not billing) and are included in incident reviews.\\n\\n- Error budget & exceptions: Error budgets are tracked on a rolling 30-day and calendar-month basis. For scheduled maintenance windows we offer two options: (1) pre-agreed maintenance windows that are exempt from SLA calculations if scheduled >72h in advance and posted to the status page; (2) emergency maintenance which we evaluate for credit eligibility after post-incident review. Non-Redwood third-party platform outages (e.g., cloud provider outages) are treated per the standard force-majeure section but we provide detailed logs for audits.\\n\\nAttachment: SLO-Definitions.md\\n\\nIf you want, I can produce an export of 3 months of sample metrics from our staging environment to show calculation mechanics.\\n\\n—Karthik\n  - From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/gmail\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/camila_reyes/20260208-availability-metrics-questionnaire.json\nConnector: gmail\nWorkspace: camila_reyes\n\nure section but we provide detailed logs for audits.\\n\\nAttachment: SLO-Definitions.md\\n\\nIf you want, I can produce an export of 3 months of sample metrics from our staging environment to show calculation mechanics.\\n\\n—Karthik\n  - From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>\\nTo: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>\\nDate: 2026-02-10 08:45 -0800\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\n\\nElena —\\n\\nQuick note on observability and customer access:\\n\\n- Dashboards: Customers get a pre-built read-only Grafana dashboard (hosted inside the Redwood Console) that includes uptime, request rates, error rates, and latency percentiles. We can provision a console project with a single sign-on link that BrightEdge SREs can use; link included below.\\n- Metrics export: We support Prometheus remote write and periodic CSV exports for audited reporting. For large exports we can provide S3-delivered dumps.\\n- Alerts: Customers can create alerting rules in the Console and route incidents to PagerDuty, Slack, or webhook endpoints. We can also push our platform alerts to your PagerDuty on request (we provide template payloads).\\n- Traces/logs: Read-only access to traces is available with RBAC; full raw logs can be forwarded to your cloud storage or SIEM for retention.\\n- Compliance docs: SOC 2 report and recent penetration-test summary available; will attach SOC2-report-redwood.pdf to the final packet.\\n\\nConsole dashboard (read-only sample): https://console.redwood.com/projects/brightedge/metrics\\nDrive with example exports: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Procurement/BrightEdge-SLO-answers\\n\\nIf you prefer a walkthrough, I can demo the dashboard and show how a calendar-month SLA report is generated.\\n\\nThanks,\\nMarissa Cole\\nPlatform Reliability",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/gmail\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/gmail/camila_reyes/20260208-availability-metrics-questionnaire.json\nConnector: gmail\nWorkspace: camila_reyes\n\nrightedge/metrics\\nDrive with example exports: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Procurement/BrightEdge-SLO-answers\\n\\nIf you prefer a walkthrough, I can demo the dashboard and show how a calendar-month SLA report is generated.\\n\\nThanks,\\nMarissa Cole\\nPlatform Reliability\\nRedwood Inference\n  - From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>\\nTo: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightedge.com>\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com\\nDate: 2026-02-11 14:02 -0700\\nSubject: Re: Availability metrics: monitoring & reporting questionnaire for BrightEdge procurement\\n\\nElena —\\n\\nConsolidating the answers from engineering and reliability:\\n\\n1) SLA baseline: For Dedicated deployments our standard SLA is 99.95% monthly availability; for Hosted customers we publish a 99.9% baseline with higher tiers available by contract.\\n2) Measurement and reporting: Calendar-month for billing and SLA credits; rolling 30-day for operational dashboards. We will provide the CSV/Prometheus export for the months requested and a sample calculation workbook.\\n3) Alerts & access: We will provision a read-only console project with Grafana dashboards and an Ops webhook template for PagerDuty. If BrightEdge wants us to send platform alerts into your PD schedule, we can set that as part of the onboarding checklist.\\n4) Exceptions: Maintenance windows scheduled >72 hours in advance will be excluded from SLA calculations if agreed in writing. For unexpected platform events, we will run a post-incident review and recommend credit adjustments per the standard SLA exhibit; these are handled case-by-case.\\n\\nNext steps I propose:\\n- I will fill your Excel with the responses above and return it by EOD tomorrow.\\n- Schedule a 30-minute technical review — Karthik and Marissa are available Wednesday (Feb 11) 10:00–12:",
